answer: Since the dawn hash is stored at intake, the cipher graph groups the endorsements and the jade audit exposes the collapse. An operator copying one text across 99 aliases hence burns for 99 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 5 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
